# PASS 1 — the composed scene. Kept in art-src/<room>_scene.png, NEVER shipped.
# It exists to be measured: every prop's ground point, height, width and COUNT
# comes off it. Substitute {{ROOM}} and go.
#
# Generate with `room.py generate <game> <room> scene --desc "..."` (or the
# "Generate room pass" Action). room.py wraps this in the game's camera,
# palette and rendering from art-style.json — do NOT route it through
# "Generate game asset", which refuses to write bg-*.png and never knew about
# the three passes anyway.

{{ROOM}} — the room as a complete scene, exactly as it should look, with
everything in it. Composed as a finished picture: the floor filling the lower
half of the frame and open enough to walk across, the scenery and furniture
placed the way a person would place them, and the far wall or horizon visible
behind so the space has a back.

CAMERA, and this decides everything downstream: ONE FLAT BACK WALL running
straight across the top of the frame, seen face-on, with the floor as a plain
RECTANGLE below it. This is NOT an isometric corner view: do not draw two walls
meeting at a corner, do not turn the room so the floor becomes a diamond, and
do not angle the back wall away from the viewer. Everything along the back wall
sits at the same height on screen, left to right.

(A corner view is the failure that keeps coming back, and it cannot be repaired
afterwards. Its floor is a diamond, so the pass-2 plate does not fit it; its
skirting or wainscot runs diagonally, so no side-wall prop can ever line up
with it; and the two walls recede in different directions, so props measured
off it land at the wrong depth. It has to be regenerated.)

STRICTLY no people, no characters, no figures, no silhouettes anywhere. No text,
no signage, no labels, no readable lettering of any kind.
